phase3_findings.description: _cte_reference_ids decides CTE exclusion by source name: sqlglot's _traverse_tables overwrites a name-keyed sources entry when an unqualified CTE reference or derived table follows a same-named/aliased base table, so the base exp.Table is excluded and a SQLite catalog read (e.g. WITH sqlite_master AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM main.sqlite_master, sqlite_master; WITH c AS (SELECT 1 AS k) SELECT * FROM sqlite_master AS c, c; SELECT count(*) FROM sqlite_master, (SELECT 1 AS k) AS sqlite_master) is classified as a data query. Makes the diff-added docstring (readonly.py 140-143, 'never by name ... sqlglot renames the base-table source key') and docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md:75 untrue. No test covers the collision.

RunSqlTool's dialect must match its runner's hard-coded dialect, but only a docstring enforces it; dialect defaults to None and is a public writable attribute, and SqlRunner does not expose its dialect. A programmatic caller omitting dialect over a MySQL runner gets '# c\nSELECT ...' reported as 'row(s) affected' with rows dropped.

When RunSqlTool's dialect disagrees with the runner's, the tool returns success=True 'N row(s) affected' and silently drops result rows; no guard, log or error. Shipped server unaffected (build_agent passes URL dialect); programmatic callers affected.

Diff-added TestGuardDoesNotCrashOnPinnedSqlglot docstring (and read-only-safety.md:240) says the deny-walk's exp.Alter entry still rejects ALTER, but test_nested_alter_still_rejected sends a root-level ALTER rejected by the root-type gate (readonly.py:590) before the deny-walk (line 599); the test passes with exp.Alter removed from _DML_DDL_TYPES.

first_sql_keyword dialect resolution: an unknown dialect silently becomes the generic tokenizer with no log (sibling is_introspection_query logs WARNING); Dialect.get(None/unknown) also scans entry_points and attempts an import on every call.
first_sql_keyword's '' covers no token, non-word first token and TokenError; it also returns any unquoted identifier while called a keyword.
first_sql_keyword docstring says '#' opens a comment only for mysql; BigQuery and ClickHouse tokenizers also treat '#' as a comment. Behavior-inert prose cap applied.

Garbled pyproject comment about first_sql_keyword vs _mysql_parse_sql disagreement; _cte_reference_ids docstring omits in-place normalization and its log names scope analysis when normalization raised. Behavior-inert prose cap applied.
Scope-analysis fallback log records only the exception type at INFO; matches criterion, missing context.
Empty-SQL check uses str.strip(), so comment-only SQL reaches the runner and with read_only off is reported as a green '1 row(s) affected'. Pre-existing.
first_sql_keyword and is_read_shaped tokenize the same SQL twice (same in is_introspection_query).

report:
## Verdict: REJECT (self-contradicting diff: two comments this PR adds describe behavior the code at HEAD does not have)

This PR is not ready to merge: the classifier's CTE exclusion can hide a real SQLite catalog table, and the docstring and internal doc this PR adds say it cannot; the new ALTER test docstring also claims coverage the test does not give.
Rule applied: self-contradicting-diff carve-out — a comment or doc line the PR's own diff added is untrue at HEAD → REJECT at every threshold

## Code Review Findings

### 🟠 Important / Major

1. `src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py` lines 149-150 (`_cte_reference_ids`): the CTE exclusion is decided by source name, not by node identity, so a real SQLite catalog table can be counted as a CTE reference and the query treated as a data query. sqlglot's `_traverse_tables` stores sources in a dict keyed by name and overwrites an entry when an unqualified CTE reference or a derived table comes after a base table with the same name or alias. The overwritten base `exp.Table` is then in no scope's sources, so the function excludes it and `is_introspection_query` skips its catalog check. Inputs that hit this: `WITH sqlite_master AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM main.sqlite_master, sqlite_master` (the qualified table first), `WITH c AS (SELECT 1 AS k) SELECT * FROM sqlite_master AS c, c`, and `SELECT count(*) FROM sqlite_master, (SELECT 1 AS k) AS sqlite_master`. SQLite accepts the last two and returns catalog rows. Before this change all three were introspection because of the `sqlite_` prefix, so this is a regression in the formatter's catalog-withholding check. Postgres and MySQL reject duplicate aliases. No test covers a base table whose source key collides with a CTE or derived-table alias. The same defect makes two lines this PR adds untrue: the docstring at `readonly.py` lines 140-143 ("Matching is by node identity, never by name: when a CTE and a base table share a name, sqlglot renames the base-table source key") and `docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md` line 75 ("one sharing the CTE's name … still counts"). The rename happens only when the base table comes after the CTE reference. (raised by 1/6 agents) [self-contradicting-diff carve-out] <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=not-held limb-one=not-evaluated limb-two=not-evaluated; evidence: functional-coverage gap in the classifier's CTE exclusion; falsehood demonstrated by reading sqlglot 30.26.0 optimizer/scope.py lines 949-959 and 1007 against view-head readonly.py 136-159 and read-only-safety.md:75 -->
2. `src/sqllens/agent/tools/run_sql.py` lines 29 and 38-46: `RunSqlTool` must classify with the same dialect as the runner it wraps, but only a docstring enforces that. The tool takes `dialect=None` by default and stores it as a public, writable attribute. Each runner hard-codes its own dialect (`"mysql"` in `mysql/sql_runner.py:139`, `"postgres"` in `postgres/sql_runner.py:169`, `"sqlite"` in `sqlite/sql_runner.py:150`), and `SqlRunner` does not expose it. `build_agent` keeps the two in step (`factory.py` lines 89 and 123). A programmatic caller that leaves out `dialect` does not: over a MySQL runner, `# c\nSELECT …` is streamed as a read, but the tool sees no keyword and reports "row(s) affected", dropping the rows. (raised by 1/6 agents)
3. `src/sqllens/agent/tools/run_sql.py` lines 72-74: when the tool's dialect and the runner's dialect disagree, the tool returns `success=True` with "N row(s) affected" and drops the result rows, with no log and no error. The docstring at lines 38-40 admits this can happen. This breaks the project rule that failures surface as structured signal, never as a silent success. The shipped server is not affected because `build_agent` passes the URL-derived dialect; programmatic callers are. (raised by 1/6 agents)

- VC-32: FAIL (important) — The docstring asserts that when a CTE and a base table share a name, sqlglot renames the base-table source key, as `apply_rls` in `rls.py` relies on, so matching by node identity keeps the base table counted. [src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:140]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  sqlglot optimizer/scope.py lines 945-959 (_traverse_tables): for an exp.Table, if table_name is in scope.sources (the CTE) and the table has no db, sources[source_name] = the CTE scope; elif source_name already in the local `sources`, the table is stored under find_new_name(...) (e.g. sqlite_master_2); else stored under source_name. So the rename happens only when the base table is processed AFTER the CTE reference (the claimed input `WITH sqlite_master AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM sqlite_master, main.sqlite_master` does rename; apply_rls at rls.py:275-286 relies on that case and its comment cites `FROM (SELECT 1) AS orders, orders`). The docstring at readonly.py:140-143 states it unconditionally ('when a CTE and a base table share a name, sqlglot renames the base-table source key'). Counterexample: `WITH sqlite_master AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM main.sqlite_master, sqlite_master`. The qualified base table is first, so it gets sources['sqlite_master']=Table (db set so the CTE branch is skipped, key not yet present). The following unqualified CTE reference then executes sources['sqlite_master']=scope.sources['sqlite_master'], overwriting the base table with the CTE scope. No rename occurs, and the base Table node is no longer in scope.sources.values(). In readonly.py:149-150 base_ids then lacks it and it is put in the CTE-reference set, so the real catalog table is not counted. The docstring's stated property is therefore wrong for this order, and the same overwrite undermines the identity matching it describes as safe (rls.py uses the same pattern).

  </details>

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor

1. `tests/unit/test_safety.py` lines 519-534: the `TestGuardDoesNotCrashOnPinnedSqlglot` docstring this PR adds says the deny-walk's `exp.Alter` entry still rejects ALTER, but the test does not reach the deny-walk. Its only ALTER test sends a root-level `ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN x INT`. `assert_select_only` rejects that at the root-type gate (`readonly.py` line 590) before the deny-walk at line 599 runs. The test would still pass if `exp.Alter` were removed from `_DML_DDL_TYPES`. The same claim appears in `docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md` line 240, and the older inline comment at lines 529-530 ("via a set-operation operand") has the same mismatch. (raised by 2/6 agents) [self-contradicting-diff carve-out] <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=not-held limb-one=not-evaluated limb-two=not-evaluated; evidence: functional-coverage gap in the test's claimed coverage; falsehood demonstrated by reading view-head test_safety.py 519-534 and readonly.py 590-602 -->
2. `src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py` line 61: two issues with how `first_sql_keyword` resolves its dialect. An unknown dialect name, such as a typo passed to `RunSqlTool(dialect=…)`, silently becomes the generic tokenizer, so on MySQL `#` stops being a comment. The sibling `is_introspection_query` logs the same fallback at WARNING. Separately, `sqlglot.Dialect.get` with `None` or an unknown name scans `entry_points()` and attempts an import on every call; `get_or_raise(None)` alone would return the base dialect. (raised by 2/6 agents)
3. `src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py` lines 45-79: the empty string returned by `first_sql_keyword` covers three cases: no token, a first token that is not a word, and a `TokenError`. Callers cannot tell "the tokenizer rejected this" from "this has no keyword". The function also returns any unquoted identifier (`FOO` for `foo bar`) while its summary line and the `query_type` metadata call it a keyword. (raised by 1/6 agents)
4. `src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py` lines 46-58: the `first_sql_keyword` docstring says `#` opens a comment "only for `mysql`", but the function accepts any sqlglot dialect, and sqlglot's BigQuery and ClickHouse tokenizers also treat `#` as a comment. The sentence holds for the three dialects `sqlglot_dialect_for_url` produces. (raised by 1/6 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: no mechanism disputed, first_sql_keyword uses the dialect's own tokenizer so rewording changes no output; grep of view-head for "opens a comment only for" finds only readonly.py:50, no tool or agent reads it; docstring of an installed module never printed -->
5. `pyproject.toml` lines 41-44: the comment "first_sql_keyword and the guard's _mysql_parse_sql output would disagree with the original text" is garbled. The disagreement is between `first_sql_keyword`, which tokenizes the original text and gets a `TokenError`, and the guard, which accepts the text after `_mysql_parse_sql` replaces the carriage return. `read-only-safety.md` line 52 states it correctly. The `_cte_reference_ids` docstring also leaves out that `normalize_identifiers` changes the caller's tree in place, and its log says "scope analysis failed" even when normalization raised. (raised by 1/6 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: no mechanism disputed, rewording changes no output; grep of view-head for the comment phrase finds only pyproject.toml:43, TOML comments are read by no tool; not published -->
6. `src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py` lines 151-158: the scope-analysis fallback logs only the exception type at INFO. The fallback changes what the user sees, because a data query whose CTE name starts with a catalog prefix is then withheld as introspection. That is hard to diagnose from the type alone. It matches the criterion and the sibling logs. (raised by 1/6 agents)
7. `src/sqllens/agent/tools/run_sql.py` lines 66-67: the new empty-SQL check uses `args.sql.strip()`, so comment-only SQL such as `-- c` still reaches the runner. With `read_only` off, SQLite runs it as a no-op and the tool reports a green "1 row(s) affected". This existed before the change, and the criterion names only empty and whitespace-only SQL. (raised by 1/6 agents)
8. `src/sqllens/agent/tools/run_sql.py` lines 72-74: `first_sql_keyword` and `is_read_shaped` each tokenize the same SQL, and `is_introspection_query` does the same at `readonly.py` lines 201-204. This is duplication only. (raised by 1/6 agents)

- VC-11: FAIL (suggestion) — The doc says TestGuardDoesNotCrashOnPinnedSqlglot checks the guard parses/walks cleanly on the pinned sqlglot and that its `exp.Alter` entry still rejects ALTER. [docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md:240]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The first half of the claim holds. test_trivial_select_passes (tests/unit/test_safety.py:524-526) runs SELECT 1 under 4 dialects, and there is no _ALTER_TYPE reference anywhere in the head view. The second half does not hold. test_nested_alter_still_rejected (lines 528-534) passes the root statement 'ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN x INT'. In src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:590-592 a root ALTER is not an _ALLOWED_ROOT_TYPES member, so it is rejected by the root-type gate with 'only SELECT statements are allowed (got ALTER)'. That happens before the deny-walk at line 599-602, where _DML_DDL_TYPES (which holds exp.Alter, line 279) is checked. The test therefore never reaches the exp.Alter entry. If exp.Alter were removed from _DML_DDL_TYPES, the test would still pass. The test's own comment says it uses a set-operation operand reachable from the Union root, but the SQL has no set operation. The doc's statement that the test checks 'its exp.Alter entry still rejects ALTER' is therefore untrue. Only the root-type gate is exercised.

  </details>

- VC-29: FAIL (suggestion) — The docstring asserts that `#` opens a comment only for the `mysql` dialect and that block comments nest only where the tokenizer nests them. [src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:50]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Docstring at src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:50-51 says '#' opens a comment only for mysql. sqlglot (pinned >=30.22,<31, pyproject.toml:45; checked in the 30.22 copy at .prflow/tmp/implement/304/sg3022/sqlglot) has other tokenizers that list '#': bigquery.py:180 COMMENTS = ['--', '#', ('/*','*/')] and clickhouse.py:80 COMMENTS = ['--', '#', '#!', ('/*','*/')]. So '# c\nSELECT 1' under dialect 'bigquery' or 'clickhouse' tokenizes '#' as a comment, contradicting 'only for mysql'. The nesting half is accurate in wording (NESTED_COMMENTS defaults True at tokens.py:204, overridden False in mysql/sqlite/bigquery/oracle/presto/snowflake). The code itself is correct since it uses the dialect tokenizer. Only the docstring is wrong. Note: sqlglot_dialect_for_url only returns postgres/mysql/sqlite, so shipped callers do not currently pass bigquery/clickhouse, but the public first_sql_keyword(sql, dialect) accepts any dialect name and the docstring is an absolute statement.

  </details>

### ℹ️ Informational — Deferred (4)

<details><summary>4 items</summary>

- VC-7: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — The pyproject comment asserts that sqlglot MySQL tokenizers older than 30.22 end a line comment at a carriage return, so first_sql_keyword and the guard's _mysql_parse_sql output would disagree below that floor. [pyproject.toml:41]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Mechanism verified: sqlglot (installed 30.26.0) MySQL Tokenizer sets COMMENTS_TERMINATE_AT_NEWLINE_ONLY = True (sqlglot/dialects/mysql.py:94) while the base Tokenizer default is False (tokens.py:213, 'line comments terminated only by \n, and not also by \r'), so a tokenizer without that override ends a '#'/'--' comment at a carriage return. readonly.py:487-544 _mysql_parse_sql rewrites \r inside line comments to a space (535-540), keeping first_sql_keyword/parse aligned with the original text; test_safety_limits.py:292-298 pins is_read_shaped("SELECT n FROM widgets # x\r'\n", 'mysql') with comment 'Needs sqlglot>=30.22'. (The hinted test is in tests/unit/test_safety_limits.py, not test_safety.py.) Not established: that 30.22 is the exact version that introduced the MySQL newline-only override. Only 30.26 installs were available (all worktree venvs checked have the flag) and no changelog or older sqlglot source was readable, so the precise floor boundary is unverified. Missing evidence: sqlglot 30.21 vs 30.22 mysql.py/tokens.py (or its release notes).

  </details>

- VC-9: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — The doc asserts that from sqlglot 30.22 the three dialects' tokenizers treat nested block comments as their engines do: Postgres nests, MySQL and SQLite end a comment at the first `*/`. [docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md:52]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  tests/unit/test_safety_limits.py:222-229 test_nested_block_comment_follows_engine asserts first_sql_keyword('/* a /* b */ c */ SELECT 1', d) == SELECT for postgres, C for mysql and sqlite, and readonly.py:45-79 tokenizes via the dialect's sqlglot tokenizer, so the code/test match the per-engine claim. pyproject.toml:45 pins sqlglot>=30.22,<31. But the claim is that this behavior starts at 30.22; the tokenizer behavior depends on the installed sqlglot, whose source is not in the supplied views. The only sqlglot copy found (/Users/the01geek/repos/sqllens/.venv, outside the views, version unidentified) shows NESTED_COMMENTS = True on the base tokenizer (tokens.py:207) and no per-dialect overrides, so it does not confirm mysql/sqlite end at the first */ or that 30.22 is where it changed. I did not run the test or inspect sqlglot 30.22.

  </details>

- VC-25: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — A resolved sqlglot Dialect instance exposes `tokenize(sql)` returning a list of Token objects with `token_type` and `text`, comments are not emitted as tokens, and every tokenizer failure on malformed input (unterminated string, unterminated block comment) is raised as `sqlglot.errors.TokenError`, so first_sql_keyword returns "" for those inputs and lets any other exception propagate. [src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:62]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Installed sqlglot 30.26.0 (pyproject pins >=30.22,<31). Dialect.tokenize (dialects/dialect.py:1286) returns Tokenizer.tokenize -> tokenizer_core.tokenize (tokenizer_core.py:687-701), which wraps ANY exception from _scan in TokenError, so 'every failure is TokenError' holds (the 'other exception propagates' branch is effectively unreachable). Unterminated string raises TokenError (tokenizer_core.py:1387/1398). Comments are not tokens: _scan_comment (887-954) appends to comments attached to tokens (except /*+ hints which can add a HINT token). BUT the claim's parenthetical that an unterminated block comment is raised as TokenError is false: the loop at tokenizer_core.py:912-930 just stops at end of input with no raise. So '/* x' yields no tokens (still '' from first_sql_keyword) while 'SELECT 1 /* x' yields tokens and returns 'SELECT', contradicting the docstring at readonly.py:58-59 ('unterminated string or comment' gives ''). Because the claim is partly wrong but the only broken text is the subject's own docstring (no outside requirement shown), I cannot FAIL, and cannot INVALID since the docstring contract is violated for that input.

  </details>

- VC-31: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — For each sqlglot `Scope`, `scope.sources` maps base-table source names to `exp.Table` nodes and CTE/derived-table names to `Scope` objects, and `scope.tables` lists every `exp.Table` in the scope, so tables in `scope.tables` not among the `exp.Table` source values are exactly those resolved to a CTE. [src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:149]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Read sqlglot scope.py (installed copy /Users/the01geek/repos/sqllens/.venv/.../sqlglot/optimizer/scope.py; the exact version pinned by the PR was not confirmed). Scope.tables is every exp.Table collected by walk (lines 220-225, excluding JoinHint children). _traverse_tables (922-1014) fills sources: a Table whose name is already in scope.sources with no db maps source name -> the CTE Scope (949-952); other FROM/JOIN/LATERAL tables map to the exp.Table (956-959); derived tables/UDTFs map to Scope. So the general shape in the claim holds. But 'exactly' is not strictly true: (a) a pivoted CTE reference also registers sources[pivot alias]=expression (955), putting the CTE-resolved Table into the Table values, so readonly.py:149-150 would not exclude it; (b) Table nodes not in FROM/JOIN/LATERAL (e.g. DML targets) are in scope.tables but not in sources, so they would be counted as CTE refs. Case (a) errs toward counting a table as a base table, and (b) the other way; I did not trace whether (b) is reachable for a read-only-validated statement, nor check repository rules requiring the property, so I cannot settle FAIL vs INVALID. Note the readonly.py code at 149-150 matches the claim's formula literally.

  </details>

</details>

checklist.evidence: Mechanism verified: sqlglot (installed 30.26.0) MySQL Tokenizer sets COMMENTS_TERMINATE_AT_NEWLINE_ONLY = True (sqlglot/dialects/mysql.py:94) while the base Tokenizer default is False (tokens.py:213, 'line comments terminated only by \n, and not also by \r'), so a tokenizer without that override ends a '#'/'--' comment at a carriage return. readonly.py:487-544 _mysql_parse_sql rewrites \r inside line comments to a space (535-540), keeping first_sql_keyword/parse aligned with the original text; test_safety_limits.py:292-298 pins is_read_shaped("SELECT n FROM widgets # x\r'\n", 'mysql') with comment 'Needs sqlglot>=30.22'. (The hinted test is in tests/unit/test_safety_limits.py, not test_safety.py.) Not established: that 30.22 is the exact version that introduced the MySQL newline-only override. Only 30.26 installs were available (all worktree venvs checked have the flag) and no changelog or older sqlglot source was readable, so the precise floor boundary is unverified. Missing evidence: sqlglot 30.21 vs 30.22 mysql.py/tokens.py (or its release notes).

checklist.evidence: The first half of the claim holds. test_trivial_select_passes (tests/unit/test_safety.py:524-526) runs SELECT 1 under 4 dialects, and there is no _ALTER_TYPE reference anywhere in the head view. The second half does not hold. test_nested_alter_still_rejected (lines 528-534) passes the root statement 'ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN x INT'. In src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:590-592 a root ALTER is not an _ALLOWED_ROOT_TYPES member, so it is rejected by the root-type gate with 'only SELECT statements are allowed (got ALTER)'. That happens before the deny-walk at line 599-602, where _DML_DDL_TYPES (which holds exp.Alter, line 279) is checked. The test therefore never reaches the exp.Alter entry. If exp.Alter were removed from _DML_DDL_TYPES, the test would still pass. The test's own comment says it uses a set-operation operand reachable from the Union root, but the SQL has no set operation. The doc's statement that the test checks 'its exp.Alter entry still rejects ALTER' is therefore untrue. Only the root-type gate is exercised.

checklist.claim: A resolved sqlglot Dialect instance exposes `tokenize(sql)` returning a list of Token objects with `token_type` and `text`, comments are not emitted as tokens, and every tokenizer failure on malformed input (unterminated string, unterminated block comment) is raised as `sqlglot.errors.TokenError`, so first_sql_keyword returns "" for those inputs and lets any other exception propagate.
checklist.verify_hint: Check `Dialect.tokenize` in sqlglot/dialects/dialect.py and `Tokenizer.tokenize` / `_scan_comment` / `_scan_string` in sqlglot/tokens.py for the raised exception type (TokenError) and whether comments become tokens or are attached to `Token.comments`
checklist.evidence: Installed sqlglot 30.26.0 (pyproject pins >=30.22,<31). Dialect.tokenize (dialects/dialect.py:1286) returns Tokenizer.tokenize -> tokenizer_core.tokenize (tokenizer_core.py:687-701), which wraps ANY exception from _scan in TokenError, so 'every failure is TokenError' holds (the 'other exception propagates' branch is effectively unreachable). Unterminated string raises TokenError (tokenizer_core.py:1387/1398). Comments are not tokens: _scan_comment (887-954) appends to comments attached to tokens (except /*+ hints which can add a HINT token). BUT the claim's parenthetical that an unterminated block comment is raised as TokenError is false: the loop at tokenizer_core.py:912-930 just stops at end of input with no raise. So '/* x' yields no tokens (still '' from first_sql_keyword) while 'SELECT 1 /* x' yields tokens and returns 'SELECT', contradicting the docstring at readonly.py:58-59 ('unterminated string or comment' gives ''). Because the claim is partly wrong but the only broken text is the subject's own docstring (no outside requirement shown), I cannot FAIL, and cannot INVALID since the docstring contract is violated for that input.

checklist.claim: For each sqlglot `Scope`, `scope.sources` maps base-table source names to `exp.Table` nodes and CTE/derived-table names to `Scope` objects, and `scope.tables` lists every `exp.Table` in the scope, so tables in `scope.tables` not among the `exp.Table` source values are exactly those resolved to a CTE.
checklist.verify_hint: Check `Scope.sources`, `Scope.tables` and `_traverse_tables` in sqlglot/optimizer/scope.py for how CTE references and base tables are stored
checklist.evidence: Read sqlglot scope.py (installed copy /Users/the01geek/repos/sqllens/.venv/.../sqlglot/optimizer/scope.py; the exact version pinned by the PR was not confirmed). Scope.tables is every exp.Table collected by walk (lines 220-225, excluding JoinHint children). _traverse_tables (922-1014) fills sources: a Table whose name is already in scope.sources with no db maps source name -> the CTE Scope (949-952); other FROM/JOIN/LATERAL tables map to the exp.Table (956-959); derived tables/UDTFs map to Scope. So the general shape in the claim holds. But 'exactly' is not strictly true: (a) a pivoted CTE reference also registers sources[pivot alias]=expression (955), putting the CTE-resolved Table into the Table values, so readonly.py:149-150 would not exclude it; (b) Table nodes not in FROM/JOIN/LATERAL (e.g. DML targets) are in scope.tables but not in sources, so they would be counted as CTE refs. Case (a) errs toward counting a table as a base table, and (b) the other way; I did not trace whether (b) is reachable for a read-only-validated statement, nor check repository rules requiring the property, so I cannot settle FAIL vs INVALID. Note the readonly.py code at 149-150 matches the claim's formula literally.

checklist.claim: The docstring asserts that when a CTE and a base table share a name, sqlglot renames the base-table source key, as `apply_rls` in `rls.py` relies on, so matching by node identity keeps the base table counted.

Matching is by node
    identity, never by name: when a CTE and a base table share a name, sqlglot

checklist.verify_hint: Check how `Scope` stores a base table whose name collides with a CTE in sqlglot/optimizer/scope.py, and whether `apply_rls` in src/sqllens/safety/rls.py relies on that renaming; falsifying input: `WITH sqlite_master AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM sqlite_master, main.sqlite_master` on sqlite
checklist.evidence: sqlglot optimizer/scope.py lines 945-959 (_traverse_tables): for an exp.Table, if table_name is in scope.sources (the CTE) and the table has no db, sources[source_name] = the CTE scope; elif source_name already in the local `sources`, the table is stored under find_new_name(...) (e.g. sqlite_master_2); else stored under source_name. So the rename happens only when the base table is processed AFTER the CTE reference (the claimed input `WITH sqlite_master AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM sqlite_master, main.sqlite_master` does rename; apply_rls at rls.py:275-286 relies on that case and its comment cites `FROM (SELECT 1) AS orders, orders`). The docstring at readonly.py:140-143 states it unconditionally ('when a CTE and a base table share a name, sqlglot renames the base-table source key'). Counterexample: `WITH sqlite_master AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM main.sqlite_master, sqlite_master`. The qualified base table is first, so it gets sources['sqlite_master']=Table (db set so the CTE branch is skipped, key not yet present). The following unqualified CTE reference then executes sources['sqlite_master']=scope.sources['sqlite_master'], overwriting the base table with the CTE scope. No rename occurs, and the base Table node is no longer in scope.sources.values(). In readonly.py:149-150 base_ids then lacks it and it is put in the CTE-reference set, so the real catalog table is not counted. The docstring's stated property is therefore wrong for this order, and the same overwrite undermines the identity matching it describes as safe (rls.py uses the same pattern).
